author: Mark Greenberg
text:
Walt -

I know you have not been talking to me about this, but, I thought you might like to have the opportunity to.  With your hay shipping season coming up - I would like to make sure you have the opportunity to use some of the truckload capacity we have available for you.  

I know that in the past you have only used some of the capacity we have been able to offer and I would like to have the opportunity to get the entire amount of truckload capacity that you need.  I have been working with the folks here at the Kansas City location to see if I can get them to commit the equipment we have available to you.  I know that is not the way you do business, but, I am trying to get it done.  

If you would like, I can give you a call next week and we can see if I can get you the equipment you need.  I know that it would be difficult for you to spend the time to do this, but, I am trying to get you the equipment you need.  I think that you know what I am saying.

text:
Tony -

I understand that you are not very computer savvy and I don't want you to think I am trying to trick you - I am not.  I have put in a little more work on this one to make it easier for you.  If I have done my job right, you will be able to figure this out on your own.  If not, I will be happy to give you a quick call and walk you through it.  Either way, I am hoping you will at least respond to this email with the right person.  I have already been told by some of my other customers that I have to be a little careful about how I go about this.  If you have any questions, please feel free to let me know.  I would also like to thank you for your business and look forward to being able to help you.  I also appreciate you taking the time to respond to my previous email.

author: Scott Govenar
text:
Listed below is a brief description of SB 1540 (Sher) relating to dams.
We should keep an eye on this throughout the session.


The bill would enact the California Dam Decommission, River Restoration,
and Public Safety Act of 2000, which would require the Secretary of
Resources, on or before January 1, 2002, to prepare and submit to the
Governor and the Legislature a report evaluating the suitability or
nonsuitability for decommission, demolition, removal, or modification of
dams, diversions, and other impoundment facilities for the purpose of
restoring spawning habitat for salmon and steelhead fisheries within the
system and within other rivers and streams in California.
